title: Cost Sculptor: Per-route & Per-customer Segmentation Autotuner
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build an automated recommendation and safe-apply system that produces per-customer and per-route batching/caching profiles. The 'Cost Sculptor' autotuner will analyze telemetry, simulate economics and latency impact, propose conservative allowlists/denylists and tiered presets, and perform guarded config applies with canarying and automatic rollback triggers. This ticket scopes the initial algorithm, evaluation harness, safe-apply orchestration, and operator-facing runbook. The outcome should reduce per-token cost for eligible customers by at least 12% in median cases while keeping P95 latency regressions <= 5% and error rate delta <= 0.05%.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The autotuner runs offline simulations on a week's worth of route/customer telemetry and emits a ranked list of recommended profiles (batch size, cache TTL, prefix allowlist, denylist) for at least 80% of active routes. 2) A canary-apply mechanism can safely apply recommendations to a small percentage of traffic and revert automatically on defined SLO breaches. 3) Production dashboard shows before/after cost and latency comparisons for canaries. 4) Unit/integration tests cover simulation correctness, policy serialization, and rollback hooks. 5) Documentation and operator runbook published to Console runbooks and linked in PR.
design_decisions: - Use existing telemetry pipeline (per-token latency histograms, KV cache hit rates, model sequence-length distributions) as primary inputs to the simulator. - Simulation will run a micro-batching cost model + tail-latency estimator rather than end-to-end traffic replay to keep runs performant. - Recommendations are expressed as named 'presets' (e.g., sculptor-conservative, sculptor-balanced, sculptor-aggressive). - Each preset maps to a safety envelope: max added latency (ms), max error budget delta, and allowed routes/customers. - Safe-apply uses a three-phase rollout: dry-run (no traffic), canary (1% traffic), ramp (10% then 50%), with automated rollback on telemetry thresholds. - Allowlist/denylist rules are prioritized: explicit customer allowlist > route-level allowlist > tier defaults. - Auditing events are emitted for every proposed and applied change for compliance and postmortem analysis.
implementation_plan: 1) Data ingest shim (2d): assemble fields needed for simulation from traces and metrics. 2) Cost & latency simulator (4d): implement micro-batch cost model + tail estimator. 3) Recommendation engine (3d): choose presets and ranked suggestions. 4) Safety policy generator (2d): build safety envelopes and create policy manifests. 5) Orchestrator & apply flow (5d): implement dry-run, canary, ramp, rollback hooks. 6) Dashboard & runbook (3d): surface suggestions, canary metrics, and operator controls. 7) End-to-end tests and load validation (4d). Total ~23d (parallelize tasks across 3 engineers).
testing_plan: - Unit tests for simulator math against synthetic workloads. - Integration test: feed recorded telemetry to the recommendation engine and assert output stability across seed changes. - Canary test in staging: apply sculptor-conservative to internal test customers and validate latency/cost deltas. - Chaos test: inject simulated slow kernels and verify rollback triggers within configured windows. - Regression: ensure existing per-route presets are not widened without explicit approval. - Performance: ensure recommendation job completes for 7 days of telemetry in < 15 minutes on our analysis infra.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha on dev orgs (1 week). Phase 1: Staging canaries on 2 internal routes with monitoring dashboards (2 weeks). Phase 2: Limited customer beta opt-in (10 customers across three tiers) with human-in-loop approval for applies (4 weeks). Phase 3: Gradual auto-opt-in for low-risk routes with sculptor-conservative preset and monthly audit (ongoing). Each apply must include 'why' string and takes place during low-traffic windows unless explicitly approved. Manual rollback button available in Console; automated rollback triggers described in monitoring_and_rollback.
monitoring_and_rollback: Telemetry to monitor per-canary: P50/P95/P99 latency, KV cache hit rate, per-token cost estimate, request error rate, tail CPU/GPU utilization. Automated rollback triggers: - P95 latency increase > 5% vs baseline sustained for 10 minutes - error rate delta > 0.05% sustained for 5 minutes - per-token cost regression > 3% for high-priority customers - unexpected increase in GPU utilization causing queueing events. Rollback behavior: immediate revert of policy to previous preset, emit incident ticket with autotuner diff, mark suggestion as 'rejected' and notify SRE/PM. All rollbacks are logged with timestamp, actor (system or user), and reason.

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive batching/caching yields larger unit savings but increases risk for tail latency and cache poisoning on noisy customers. We prioritize conservative default to avoid customer impact and escalate to more aggressive presets via opt-in or explicit SRE signoff. Future work: integrate with Optimize's quantization recommendations and include ML-based prediction of SLO impact for each route.
